topic.title: Curvature-Aware and Structured Optimization
topic.overview: These methods improve learning by exploiting objective structure beyond an ordinary gradient step. Representatives estimate curvature efficiently, combine stochastic and quasi-Newton updates, handle nonconvex regularizers, and optimize nested objectives. The goal is useful directional information without the cost of explicitly storing or inverting a full Hessian.
topic.whyItMatters: Faster convergence is valuable only if obtaining each update does not consume the savings. Low-dimensional approximations, reused gradients, and parallel estimation can make second-order ideas practical, but their accuracy depends on the problem structure.
topic.evolution: Early work estimates Hessian eigenvectors for learning-rate selection. Later methods maintain tractable curvature approximations and study hybrid optimization. Recent bilevel algorithms use empirical Fisher information and synchronized inner updates to reduce hypergradient cost. The collection shows recurring efforts to balance more informative steps against memory, sampling, and implementation overhead.
openQuestions: When do cheap curvature surrogates preserve the directions that matter most?
How can nested optimization distinguish approximation error from incomplete inner convergence?
